notes.fact: Three-way talks between Russia, Ukraine and the US opened in Abu Dhabi on Tuesday, according to the head of Kyiv's delegation, Rustem Umerov.
NBC says the two-day session is the first of its kind since February and will centre on security guarantees, and that no signs of the fighting abating were seen.
Kushner told the opening session that Washington has found where gaps remain and has ideas to bridge them; Russian state media announced the start of talks.
PTI (India) reports the Abu Dhabi talks as a US-brokered push, noting Putin rejects a general halt in hostilities while Zelenskyy rejects ceding territory.
Russia's foreign minister Lavrov says security issues are top of the agenda and the aim is agreeing principles; Moscow says the format stays trilateral, without Europeans.
Ukraine's energy ministry says Russian strikes overnight left some consumers without power in six regions, including Kyiv, with emergency outages applied in Kyiv, Kharkiv, Poltava and Sumy.
Ukrenergo, the grid operator, says Russia hit energy sites in eight regions overnight, including substations, heating plants and oil and gas facilities.
The IAEA says a drone attack on Monday killed an employee at the Russian-held Zaporizhzhia nuclear plant, and another worker at the nearby thermal plant.
The plant's Russian-installed management blamed Ukraine for the death; the IAEA does not assign responsibility and gave no details on who flew the drone.
The plant lost its sole 330 kV external line for about 10 hours on Nov 8 and ran on emergency diesel generators until power returned.
After meeting Qatar's prime minister, Trump said Iran is militarily 'effectively over' and the US is keeping the status quo, including the naval blockade and a new Task Force Iron Gate.

notes.fact: Trump told reporters military action 'doesn't seem to be a very necessary thing' but the US is 'locked and loaded'; he kept open the possibility of new strikes.
notes.key: claim:us president us is a combatant

notes.fact: Iran's security council secretary Mohsen Rezaei dismissed talk of negotiations as invented and told Washington to accept Iran's seven conditions, including lifting the blockade and sanctions.
The Logical Indian reports Iran sent a nuclear proposal to Washington via Qatar on Nov 5, citing a senior Iranian official to Reuters; Tehran says talks start only after its conditions are met.
Houseofsaud, a low-profile site, says no ceasefire exists, the blockade runs and Rubio called Iran's terms unrealistic; claims cite The National and are not independently checked.
The Wall Street Journal reported US refuelling tankers left RAF Mildenhall on Monday after a purported Iranian threat; its nature is still under discussion among US officials.
Sky News counted 12 aircraft, nine tankers and three Ospreys, leaving Mildenhall; Britain's defence ministry said aircraft move regularly according to operational needs.
The National, citing a US official, says security at RAF Mildenhall and RAF Lakenheath was raised to FPCON Charlie, the second-highest US force-protection level.
UKMTO's weekly report counted 325 Hormuz transits, about 65% below pre-conflict levels, with at least 11 ships attacked in the week to Nov 6 and three sunk.
Middle East Eye reports UKMTO logged 11 attacks in the seven days to Nov 4, including a dhow strike that killed one crew member, and none on Red Sea shipping.
Iran's Revolutionary Guards say two tankers hit mines on unauthorised routes; Russian outlet TASS relays UKMTO's report of one tanker on fire and one struck, crews safe.

notes.fact: Fox News says war fallout, including high gas prices, is blamed as a key factor in Republican losses in last Tuesday's midterm elections.
notes.event: US midterms and Iran war politics

notes.fact: Rep. Massie filed eight articles of impeachment against Hegseth, including the Caribbean boat strikes; a House vote is required within two legislative days, by Wednesday at the latest.
Axios says GOP leaders are bracing for enough defections to impeach; it notes Senate removal would be very hard even with a Democratic majority from January.
The Saudi-led coalition says it intercepted two missiles fired at Riyadh, a ballistic missile aimed at the south and a drone over the Eastern Province.
Al Jazeera says the Riyadh interceptions came hours after damage was reported to the East-West pipeline, a key Saudi export route while Hormuz is restricted.
Reuters says hostilities rose after the Houthis advanced toward the Bab el-Mandeb Strait in September, and the group has since hit Saudi airports, ports and oil sites.
The coalition says it destroyed two Houthi factories making missile parts and fuel, and Canada's prime minister condemned the Houthi attacks in a call with the Saudi crown prince.
notes.event: Coalition strikes on Houthi missile sites

notes.fact: The National says the coalition downed two ballistic and two cruise missiles aimed at Riyadh; Houthi spokesman Saree claimed attacks on a Riyadh airport and Aramco sites, and a UN-brokered 2022 truce is broken.

notes.fact: French foreign minister Barrot says Iran's Revolutionary Guards carried out the October attack on supermarket fridges, and France summoned Iran's ambassador; Iran had not publicly replied in reports seen.

notes.fact: Paris prosecutors opened an investigation into Shahid Kaveh, an IRGC-linked cyber unit; the attack hit about 700 sites on Oct 11-12, with temperatures raised to 50C in some stores.
notes.event: France attributes fridge hack to IRGC

notes.fact: CNBC reports France is 'not ruling anything out' in response and puts the damage at millions of euros; the attribution is France's assessment, not a court finding.

notes.fact: BigGo Finance says a French report names three IRGC officials and puts spoiled food in the tens of millions of euros, with at least 15 fires; evidence not published.

notes.fact: CISA, FBI, HHS, USDA and DOT warned that attackers target unpatched or internet-exposed refrigeration controllers, advising removal from the internet, new passwords and patches; no vendor or attacker named.
A security blog says SOCRadar found the same controller families exposed in the US on Nov 5, and no civilian US incident had been reported by Nov 9; lower-reliability source.

CSIS records that Iran-linked CyberAv3ngers claimed August attacks on US water systems in at least a dozen states; the US government has not publicly attributed them, and drinking water quality was not broadly affected.
A tracker lists a Oct 26 cyberattack on the University of New Mexico Health System; no new details or attribution were found in the last 48 hours.
